chunk_findings.detail: `_carry_reviewer` uses `prior.get("model")` as the *sole* trigger for copying the entire reviewer identity in `_REVIEWER_KEYS`, so identity is only carried (or dropped) as a unit keyed on one of its four fields. Two inputs fall through badly. (a) A caller who restates a reviewer field other than `model` gets a hybrid identity stitched from two rounds: with prior `{"model": "deepseek-v3", "family": "deepseek", "reviewer": "lan-deepseek", "reviewed_sha": "abc1234"}` and a hand record `{"family": "openai"}` (i.e. `gate record critic --outcome passed --family openai`), the outer guard is true, `family` is skipped because it is in `evidence`, and `model`/`reviewer` are copied from the prior round, yielding `{family: "openai", model: "deepseek-v3", reviewer: "lan-deepseek", ...}` — a record that attributes the review to an openai-family reviewer with a deepseek model, and that any consumer resolving the reviewer from `model` (the very field this bug is about, and the one the docstring admits can be overridden by a stale complement) reads as the stale deepseek identity. (b) When the prior round recorded identity without a `model` key at all (e.g. `{"reviewer": "lan-deepseek", "family": "deepseek", "reviewed_sha": "abc1234"}`, which the `reviewer`-named field in the bug report suggests is possible), the guard is false and no reviewer is carried, so the original failure survives: the hand pass record has no reviewer and `complete` still refuses with "reviewer independence not satisfied". The explicit-`model` branch already implements the correct rule for one key — an explicitly stated part of the identity must suppress the rest of the prior identity, and any identity key present in `prior` should be carried when the new record states none — so the fix should be applied per key over `_REVIEWER_KEYS` rather than gated on `prior.get("model")`.
